Front: What is the exact mathematical difference between Covariate Shift (Data Drift) and Concept Drift?
Back: Covariate Shift: P(X) changes while P(Y|X) remains constant (input distribution shifts, but feature-to-label mapping holds). Concept Drift: P(Y|X) changes (the conditional probability distribution of targets given inputs changes, e.g. spam/fraud definitions shift).

Front: In GCP Vertex AI Model Monitoring, how does Training-Serving Skew differ from Prediction Drift?
Back: Training-Serving Skew (Feature Skew) compares live production serving features against the baseline training dataset. Prediction Drift (Serving Drift) compares live serving features/predictions across two consecutive production time windows (e.g., current 48h vs. previous 48h).

Front: What is the exact execution order of operations when sampling a token from an LLM?
Back: 1) Logits scaled by temperature (z/T) then Softmax -> 2) Truncate low-probability tokens via top-k (fixed count) and/or top-p (cumulative mass) and renormalize -> 3) Sample next token from remaining distribution.

Front: What is the exact definition of top-p (nucleus sampling), and why is the candidate pool size dynamic?
Back: top-p selects the smallest set of most-probable tokens whose cumulative probability mass sums to >= p. The set size is dynamic because it contracts to 1-2 tokens when the model is confident and expands to many tokens when the distribution is flat/uncertain.

Front: Why does setting temperature = 0 render top-k and top-p sampling completely irrelevant?
Back: At temperature = 0, Softmax collapses into a deterministic argmax (step function) where the top token has probability 1.0 (100%) and all others 0.0. The top token trivially satisfies p >= 1.0 and k >= 1, so top-k and top-p never filter anything.

Front: Which Prometheus metric type (Counter, Gauge, Histogram) should be used for: 1) Total Requests, 2) Drift Score (PSI), 3) Inference Latency?
Back: 1) Counter: monotonically increasing count for Total Requests. 2) Gauge: value that fluctuates up and down for Drift Score / PSI. 3) Histogram: samples into configurable buckets to calculate percentiles (p50, p99) for Inference Latency.

Front: What statistical distance/test is typically used for numerical features vs. categorical features in drift detection (Evidently / Vertex AI)?
Back: Numerical features: Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test, Wasserstein distance, or binned Population Stability Index (PSI). Categorical features: Chi-squared (chi^2) test or Population Stability Index (PSI).
